categories.name: Final Value
categories.description: Your character receives one final value. It might reflect the career events you chose, or some other element of who they have become.

categories.name: Attributes
categories.description: Bring any attribute over the limits back within them, then increase two attributes by 1 each without going over the limits. This fixes your final attribute scores.

categories.name: Departments
categories.description: Bring any department over the limits back within them, then increase two departments by 1 each without going over the limits. This fixes your final department scores.

categories.name: Talent
categories.description: Choose one extra talent, bringing you to a total of four. Its requirements are checked against your final scores.

categories.name: Portrait
categories.description: Choose a portrait that represents your character. It is shown in the character summary and has no game-rule effect.

categories.name: Name & Pronouns
categories.description: Name your character and record their pronouns and age. Pronouns help others use the proper address for your character.

categories.name: Pastime
categories.description: Optional: a hobby or passion your character enjoys when off duty. It has no rule effect in this prototype.

categories.name: Background Notes
categories.description: Optional notes about your character's history and personality. Free text that is saved with the character but never used by the game rules.

notes: Prototype: cards follow the unlock order, with Name & Pronouns as the last required choice and the optional Background Notes after it.

The Talent card comes from Star Trek Adventures 2E (Core p.132: 'select one extra talent, bringing you to a total of four'); it follows Disciplines so talent requirements are checked against final scores.
Screen 07 is Book Step Seven. Assignment and Rank from Step Seven are on Screen 05.

Prototype: Name (required), Portrait (required), and Background Notes (optional) are videogame additions. The book's lifepath has no naming step. Pronouns are from p.132 and, as in the book, required.
Player-facing text never labels anything as a book rule, adaptation, or original system; provenance stays in data (sourceType) and these notes.
Designer decision (Oct 2026): the mockup's Service Motto and Personal Goals are dropped from the design (Service Motto would duplicate Values).

Order follows Core p.132: first any score over the limits (12 / 5 with only one at the maximum; 11 / 4 with Untapped Potential) is reduced and each reduced point is given to another score within the limits; then the two +1s are added, and a +1 can't take a score over the limits (nor make a second score reach the maximum).
Implementation pick (book silent): when two or more scores are at or above the maximum, the player chooses which one keeps the maximum; the others drop to one below it.

Designer decision (Oct 2026): as soon as lifepath scores go over the limits (a change on an earlier screen), the game places a default the player can change, so the screen never stalls waiting on it: the highest tied score keeps the maximum, and each reduced point goes to the lowest score that can take it (list order breaks ties). The card says what was moved.

Age (Core p.132 Personal Details, guidance in the p.127 sidebar) is optional free text stored as identity.age; the guidance for the chosen Experience is shown as help. Pastime (Core pp.132-133) is optional free text stored as identity.pastime; the book gives it no fixed rule effect (the gamemaster may let it act as a focus when relevant), so the prototype gives it none.
The mockup's Randomize category is replaced by the per-screen Auto button. Category images point into public/; missing files fall back to the placeholder portrait.
